findings.claim: kvstore/src/storage.rs line 3 declares `use crate::api::Response;`, an upward import from the storage layer into the api layer. ADR-0001 (Accepted) states: "Dependencies flow strictly downward: `api` may use `cache`, `cache` may use `storage`, and `storage` depends on nothing inside this crate. Upward imports (e.g. `storage` importing `api`) are prohibited." This is the exact prohibited case named in the decision, and rust-analyzer records the edge (file:kvstore/src/storage.rs imports api/ and api/Response#). It is also the only crate-internal import in storage.rs.

`FileStore::status_response` (kvstore/src/storage.rs:33-39) is a public method of the storage layer whose return type is the wire-protocol enum `api::Response`, constructing `Response::Ok` and `Response::Error` directly. This places wire-protocol formatting in the storage layer and is the reason the upward import in F-0001 exists: the boundary breach is in storage's published API surface, not only in its import list. ADR-0001's stated consequence is that "the storage layer stays reusable and testable without wire-protocol types" (REQ-005 acceptance criterion: "storage is usable and testable without wire-protocol types"); a caller cannot use this method without linking the api layer.

The downward composition the layering commits to is absent: nothing in the crate depends on `storage`. `cache.rs` imports only `std` (lines 3-4) and never references `FileStore`; `api::handle_request` reaches only `Cache::get`/`Cache::put` (kvstore/src/api.rs:15-33) and stores values solely in the in-memory map. The only crate-internal edge touching storage runs upward (storage -> api), and `FileStore` is referenced nowhere outside its own module and the `pub use` at lib.rs:10. This contradicts the structure stated in REQ-007 — "an in-memory cache in front of a file-backed store", with the acceptance criterion "values are persisted to a file-backed store, not held only in memory" — and inverts the direction ADR-0001 prescribes (`cache` may use `storage`).
